main_text.p: nio Ælianus: Σωιάσι γὰρ ἐλέφαντες καὶ γλώττης ἀνθρωπίνης τῆς ἐπιχωρίας, Capiunt ser humanum sermonem elephantes, sed indigenam. Et Dio: ἠδὴ καὶ ἐκεῖνο εἶπον, τῆς φωνῆς τῆς πατρῴωτιδ᾽ αὐτὸς ἐπαίειν, Et jam hoc ajunt, eos patriam vocem audire atque intelligere. Quippe institutio eorum lingua fit. Vnde idem Ælianus: Docentur atque instituuntur ad varia φωνὴ τινὶ ὑπηχωείῳ, ὥσπερ οὖν ἐλλήχασι, φύσει τινὶ, ἀπὸ ῥήτωρ καὶ μάλισα γε ἰδίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦδε, sermone vernaculo, cujus miro quodam, ser ineffabili modo, ac peculiari, naturā sunt capaces.
Succinit his Oppianus, elephantes inter se colloqui diserte scribens:
main_text.l: Φήμη δ᾽ ὡς ἐλέφαντες ἐπ᾽ ἀλλήλοις λαλέου-

l.i: Fama est, inter sese sermocinari elephantes,

main_text.p: Christophorus sanè Acosta, Hispanus, qui novum illum Orbis tractum, quem Orientalem Indiam vocant; in quo elephantum omnia plena ipse vidit & lustravit, nihil certius in regno Malabar esse testatur, quàm quòd hæ belluæ communicent inter se ser-

page.notes: Greek text is partly set in a noticeably worn or doubtful state; the Greek readings above are best effort and may contain errors. Several Latin words are blurred by show-through and page damage, notably "Vnde" and "Distinctasque". Line "Φθογγὴν … θείῃ / ζοῦσες" is uncertain. Last line ends mid-word ("ser-") and continues on the next page.
